requirements.language_requirement: English CEFR C1 or IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 88
requirements.tuition_fee: €6,000 per semester for non-EU students (+ €97 semester fee)
requirements.notes: Preliminary documentation (VPD) via uni-assist required prior to TUMonline application. Mandatory GRE General (min 164 Quant, 4.0 AW) for degrees from India, China, Iran, Pakistan.

statementRequirements.summary: TUM M.Sc. Informatics requires a letter of motivation (max 2 DIN A4 pages) explaining prior academic foundation, specific curricular focus at TUM, and career relevance.
statementRequirements.submissionMethod: Upload as PDF to TUMonline application portal during application window
statementRequirements.formattingRequirements: DIN A4 format, PDF file, English or German, legible standard font (11–12pt)

specificQuestions.question: What prior foundational coursework and practical experience prepare you for TUM Informatics?
specificQuestions.guidance: Highlight advanced algorithms, discrete mathematics, and software engineering projects.

specificQuestions.question: Which specific specialization areas or research chairs at TUM (e.g. Distributed Systems, AI, Robotics) do you intend to focus on and why?
specificQuestions.guidance: Cite exact TUM Informatics modules and active faculty research chairs.

specificQuestions.question: How does this degree connect to your future professional milestones or research aspirations?
specificQuestions.guidance: Connect curriculum directly to planned industry engineering roles or doctoral research.

assessmentCriteria: Demonstrated technical rigor in computer science fundamentals
Concrete alignment between undergraduate study and TUM M.Sc. Informatics syllabus
High academic writing quality and clear scholarly intent
statementRequirements.aiPolicy: Independent authorship required. Under TUM Academic Integrity regulations, automated or AI-generated text without explicit declaration violates submission rules.
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: TUM central guidance recommends concise academic justification over biographical storytelling or childhood anecdotes.

requirements.language_requirement: English B2 (IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 80) and German C1 before final enrollment
requirements.notes: Strict curricular prerequisite: 34 ECTS Practical CS, 24 ECTS Technical CS, 24 ECTS Theoretical CS, 26 ECTS Math. Mandatory GRE (Quant > 75th percentile, Verbal > 15th percentile, AW >= 3.5).

statementRequirements.summary: RWTH Aachen M.Sc. Computer Science does NOT evaluate a Statement of Purpose or Motivation Letter. Admission is determined strictly on curricular ECTS credit distribution and GRE cutoff scores.
assessmentCriteria: Curricular subject-specific ECTS match: 34 ECTS Practical CS, 24 ECTS Technical CS, 24 ECTS Theoretical CS, 26 ECTS Math
GRE General Test cutoff percentiles (Quant > 75th percentile)
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: Do not submit unsolicited motivation letters via RWTHonline as they are not evaluated by the admissions committee.
statementRequirements.statusNotes: Admission is purely based on formal academic credentials, credit equivalence, and GRE.

requirements.language_requirement: English proficiency Level B2/C1 (IELTS 6.5 with no band < 6.0 or TOEFL 90)
requirements.tuition_fee: €1,500 per semester for non-EU students (+ €189.80 semester fee)
requirements.notes: Baden-Württemberg state statutory fee applies to all non-EU students. Apply directly via heiCO portal.

statementRequirements.generalGuidance: General Heidelberg University guidelines recommend checking whether your specific study track requires a statement or work sample via the heiCO application portal.
statementRequirements.statusNotes: Programme-specific statement instructions are not confirmed in the official study handbook. Please consult the heiCO admission portal or departmental advisor.

requirements.language_requirement: English proficiency Level C1 (IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL 95)
requirements.notes: Elite network of Bavaria program. Strong background in statistics and computer science required. Direct application via LMU online portal.

statementRequirements.summary: LMU M.Sc. Data Science requires a detailed motivation letter in English (max 1,000 words) addressing statistical background and CS foundation.
statementRequirements.submissionMethod: Direct submission via LMU Elite Network portal

specificQuestions.question: Describe your quantitative and statistical background, highlighting courses in probability, inference, or linear models.
specificQuestions.guidance: Detail statistical theory and applied modeling experience.

specificQuestions.question: What programming languages and data science toolkits have you utilized in substantive software or analysis projects?
specificQuestions.guidance: Mention Python, R, C++, SQL, or distributed computing frameworks.

specificQuestions.question: Why is the Elite Network of Bavaria Data Science curriculum at LMU uniquely suited to your career aims?
specificQuestions.guidance: Connect to elite research projects and industrial internships.

assessmentCriteria: Strong mathematical and computational rigor
Proficiency in statistical modeling and algorithm implementation
Clear academic focus on data science applications
statementRequirements.aiPolicy: Applicants must submit original work. AI-assisted drafting must be disclosed.
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: LMU emphasizes demonstrating both statistical foundations and computer science skills in equal balance.
statementRequirements.statusNotes: Intake criteria under annual review by the admissions committee for the upcoming winter round.

name: Trinity College Dublin (TCD)
program: M.Sc. Computer Science (Intelligent Systems / Data Science)

requirements.notes: Requires First- or upper second-class honours degree (2:1) in CS or closely related discipline. Apply directly via my.tcd.ie (application fee €55).

statementRequirements.summary: Trinity College Dublin M.Sc. Computer Science requires a personal statement of 1–2 pages. Strand reorganization is pending review for the upcoming cycle.

specificQuestions.question: Why have you chosen your selected strand (Intelligent Systems, Data Science, Future Networked Systems, or Augmented & Virtual Reality)?
specificQuestions.guidance: State specific curriculum strand and relevant modules.

specificQuestions.question: Outline your previous academic achievements and computational coursework relevant to this strand.
specificQuestions.guidance: Emphasize NFQ Level 8 equivalent preparation and major projects.

assessmentCriteria: Academic merit and 2:1 Honours equivalent standing
Relevance of undergraduate computing degree to selected strand
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: Trinity postgraduate admissions recommend keeping the statement strictly focused on academic and professional capabilities.
statementRequirements.statusNotes: TCD strand definitions are undergoing curriculum updates. Statement prompts should be confirmed on my.tcd.ie upon portal opening.

requirements.notes: Requires NFQ Level 8 2:1 Honours in Computer Science or related degree. Direct online application via UCD Graduate Admissions portal.

statementRequirements.submissionMethod: Upload via UCD Graduate Admissions portal

specificQuestions.question: Detail your proposed negotiated learning stream and module selections across CS themes.
specificQuestions.guidance: Refer to the UCD negotiated learning stream catalog.

specificQuestions.question: How does your undergraduate foundation in computing support this specialized study plan?

assessmentCriteria: Feasibility and coherence of the proposed negotiated learning module plan
Strength of undergraduate computer science preparation
statementRequirements.aiPolicy: Original student work required under UCD Student Code.
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: UCD guidelines recommend contacting the programme director if you are unsure whether to follow the 500-word central portal limit or 2-page school format.

Contact UCD admissions before submission.

requirements.language_requirement: IELTS 6.5 overall (minimum 6.5 in writing, 6.0 other bands) or TOEFL iBT 88
requirements.notes: Requires NFQ Level 8 First Class Honours or strong 2:1 in Computer Science or quantitative STEM discipline. Apply direct via University of Galway portal.

statementRequirements.submissionMethod: University of Galway direct online portal
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: University of Galway postgraduates generally provide academic references and CV; statement requirements vary by stream and must be checked on the live portal.
statementRequirements.statusNotes: Programme-specific statement instructions are not confirmed. Check the University of Galway online application portal.

requirements.language_requirement: IELTS 6.5 overall (no individual band < 6.0) or TOEFL iBT 90
requirements.notes: Second Class Honours Grade 1 (2H1) in primary Level 8 Computer Science degree. Apply via UCCApply portal (application fee €50).

specificQuestions.guidance: Address UCC computing facilities and curriculum.

Clarity of academic intent
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: UCC admissions prefers concise statements addressing specific laboratory strengths.

name: Imperial College London
program: M.Sc. Computing (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning)

requirements.language_requirement: Higher College Requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall (min 6.5 all bands) or TOEFL iBT 100 (min 22 all bands)
requirements.notes: First-Class Honours UK Bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) with substantial computing coursework. GRE is NOT required.

statementRequirements.summary: Imperial College London M.Sc. Computing (AI and ML) requires a personal statement (1–2 pages) demonstrating computing foundations, motivation, and career direction.
statementRequirements.submissionMethod: Imperial College online postgraduate application portal
statementRequirements.formattingRequirements: PDF format, clean layout, 1.15 line spacing

specificQuestions.question: What drives your technical passion for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning?
specificQuestions.guidance: Focus on technical challenges and recent developments.

specificQuestions.question: Highlight key mathematical, programming, or systems projects you have implemented.
specificQuestions.guidance: Provide concrete metrics and architectural decisions.

specificQuestions.question: How does this taught master's prepare you for your immediate post-graduation milestones?
specificQuestions.guidance: Articulate specific career or research outcomes.

assessmentCriteria: Mathematical maturity (linear algebra, probability, multivariate calculus)
Proven programming proficiency and algorithmic problem solving
Clarity of purpose and alignment with Imperial faculty
statementRequirements.aiPolicy: Applicants must submit original work. Generating personal statements using automated LLMs or AI assistants is prohibited under Imperial College admissions conduct regulations.
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: Imperial advises candidates to be concise and fact-focused, demonstrating aptitude through concrete projects rather than general praise of the university.

requirements.language_requirement: Higher level: IELTS 7.5 (min 7.0 each component) or TOEFL iBT 110 (min 22 L, 24 R/W, 25 S)
requirements.notes: First-Class undergraduate degree in Computer Science or Mathematics. GRE/GMAT scores are explicitly NOT requested or used in admissions evaluation.

statementRequirements.summary: University of Oxford M.Sc. in Advanced Computer Science requires a concise statement of purpose (maximum 1,000 words) articulating academic readiness, theoretical depth, and research interests.
statementRequirements.submissionMethod: Upload as PDF to Oxford Graduate Application Portal
statementRequirements.formattingRequirements: Standard single PDF, 1-inch margins, minimum 11pt font

specificQuestions.question: Outline your undergraduate background in advanced mathematics and computer science.
specificQuestions.guidance: Detail rigorous math proofs, algorithms, and theory courses.

specificQuestions.question: Which specific advanced computer science topics, departmental seminars, or lab groups align with your intended focus?
specificQuestions.guidance: Cite Oxford CS Department research groups and faculty publications.

specificQuestions.question: Why is Oxford ACS the essential programme for your research or advanced technical career?
specificQuestions.guidance: State intended thesis direction or advanced industrial role.

assessmentCriteria: First-Class academic capability in computing and mathematical foundations
Articulation of mature scientific curiosity and research alignment
High standard of written academic English
statementRequirements.aiPolicy: Oxford University Statement on AI: Personal statements must be the applicant's own authentic work. Plagiarism and undeclared use of generative AI are strictly evaluated through integrity checks.
statementRequirements.generalGuidance: Oxford Department of Computer Science emphasizes that applicants should write directly about technical interests rather than flowery biographical introductions.

requirements.language_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall (no component < 6.5) or TOEFL iBT 100 (min 25 in writing, 22 other bands)
requirements.notes: UK First Class or high 2:1 Honours in Computer Science with minimum 50% core CS content. Direct online application via Manchester Graduate Admissions portal.

specificQuestions.question: Explain your motivation for pursuing Advanced Computer Science and your intended pathway (e.g., Software Engineering, AI).

specificQuestions.guidance: Summarize major project or bachelor thesis.

Coherent justification for advanced pathway modules
